name: LumenCart
summary: Shopify app from Fleeta that turns the product photos you already have into AI studio and lifestyle images, one at a time or in bulk, and publishes them to the product in one click. The per-credit rate stops improving at Pro. Launched August 2026, no reviews yet.
best_for: small Shopify merchants who want studio and lifestyle product shots out of the photos they already have, without hiring a photographer or a studio, and who want them published straight to the product rather than downloaded and re-uploaded, and who can size their month in credits, because the ladder is metered rather than featured
skip_if: you generate at high volume month after month: the per-credit rate stops improving at Pro, so a big catalogue keeps paying Pro's rate however far up the ladder you go. Skip it too if you need the highest-quality setting as your default, since it costs 2 credits an image and halves every allowance on the page, and if you want a track record before you trust AI imagery on your listings, because this app launched in August 2026 and carries a single review
honest_knock:
Two things decide whether this is cheap, and neither is the plan price. The first is that you buy credits, not images: highest quality costs 2 credits against 1 for standard, so the better setting halves every allowance on the page: Starter's 75 credits is 37 images a month, not 75.

The second is the one-off packs, which look like a convenient top-up and are the most expensive way to buy. On their own figures, 25 credits for $22 is about $0.88 a credit, while Starter's $9 for 75 is about $0.12 and Pro's $79 for 1,000 is about $0.08. A pack is roughly seven to eleven times the subscription rate per credit, so if you keep reaching for packs you are on the wrong plan. Monthly credits are described as refreshed each month with nothing said about rolling over, so assume an unused allowance is gone; the packs, by contrast, state a 12-month life.

The free tier is also smaller than it looks: 25 generations is a lifetime total for the store, not a monthly one, which is a single afternoon of trying looks across a catalogue. And the app is new, launched 8 August 2026 with a single review on its listing at the time of writing (five stars, dated 6 September 2026), so there is no real track record yet on image quality or on support.

pricing.notes:
(read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/lumencart and in our own test that day; earlier: read 22 September 2026 and re-read unchanged on 27 September and 11 November 2026 on the vendor's own pricing page, lumencart.fleeta.co.uk/pricing) Free $0 with 25 lifetime image generations for a new store; then Starter $9, Growth $29, Pro $79 and Scale $199 a month, with annual billing taking 15% off. The Shopify listing publishes only the free plan and carries no dollar amount at all — it links out to this page with “See all pricing options”, so the App Store card is half the ladder.

Read the plans in credits rather than images, because that is what you actually buy: the monthly allowances are 75, 300, 1,000 and 2,500 credits, refreshed monthly, and an image costs 1 credit at standard quality or 2 at the highest. So Starter's 75 credits is 75 standard images a month, or 37 at the better setting. Unused monthly credits do not appear to roll over — the page says refreshed monthly and says nothing about carrying them forward.

One-off credit packs sit alongside the plans and do carry a stated life: 25 credits for $22, 100 for $82, 300 for $234 and 1,000 for $749, valid for 12 months. Two things in the buyer's favour that the page states outright: technical failures and image-safety refusals do not consume credits, and the restore-point retention rises with the tier — 30, 90, 180 and 365 days. Prices are in USD and billed through Shopify, which shows the final amount before you approve it. Read again on 17 November 2026: the Shopify listing still prints only the Free plan (25 lifetime image generations, private previews before publishing, product search and multi image selection) and no dollar amount, and now shows one review, five stars, dated 6 September 2026, where our earlier readings found none. In our own test the same day on a Shopify development store the app opened on its overview with the Free plan active, no card and no plan choice, and 24 of 25 credits left after one studio image. The app's plan screen listed Free, Starter $9, Growth $29, Pro $79 and Scale $199 a month, with a 15% annual saving, matching the vendor's page. But when we chose Starter, Shopify's plan screen offered only a Free plan, marked free to test on this store with regular pricing applying when the store goes live, so the paid plans could not be selected on a development store and we saw no approval screen for them.

compare_with.name: AdCreative.ai, Retouch4me
compare_with.why:
All three put AI between you and a product image, and they sit at three different points of the job. Retouch4me, from our own dossier verified 8 September 2026, retouches photographs you already shot: Photoshop-compatible plugins on perpetual licences at $145 to $179 each, or cloud retouching in packs at $24 for 100 credits. AdCreative.ai, verified 13 September 2026, makes ad creative and banners rather than catalogue photography, metered by download from roughly $29–39 a month for 10 credits up to $1,399 for 200. LumenCart generates the scene itself (studio and lifestyle images built from the photo you have) and is the only one of the three that publishes the result to the Shopify product in one click.

So the comparison is mostly about where your bottleneck is. If you have good photographs and want them cleaner, Retouch4me is the tool and its perpetual licences mean you stop paying. If you need creative for paid campaigns, AdCreative.ai is built for that and LumenCart is not. LumenCart only wins when the photograph you want does not exist and the destination is a product listing.

On evidence the other two are ahead, and by a distance: LumenCart launched in August 2026 and has one review, five stars, from 6 September 2026. That is not a reason to rule it out at $9 a month, but it is the reason to spend the 25 free generations before you commit to a plan.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested LumenCart (an AI product photo generator) on a Shopify development store: the install without a plan choice or a card, one private preview of The Out of Stock Snowboard in the Studio (about 70 seconds, 1 credit, 99% match, a result that looked almost the same as the original), the Billing screen (25 lifetime image generations on the Free plan, 25 credits shown while the Studio showed 24), the plan window with five plans from Free to Scale at $199 a month and the Shopify Select a plan page, which offered only Free after a click on Starter. Nothing was paid, approved or published to the store. Install: the app was installed from its App Store listing (called Fleeta LumenCart: AI Photos, vendor Fleeta Limited; the app is called LumenCart in the admin) through the install form, in our own tab. The dialog Install app asked for access to View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Products, Shopify admin), and Install was clicked at about 21:52 (the app logs 17 Nov 2026, 21:52). No terms of service box, plan choice, card or phone number was asked. The app opened on Overview with the line See your first product image in a few minutes. and a counter 0/3 successful outputs. LumenCart is an AI product photo generator, not a cart drawer or an upsell app, so the core action is generating one image. Core action: Overview, Start with one product, Studio, the product The Out of Stock Snowboard (1 source image, 80% baseline), the mode Keep product details (the default), Standard at 1 credit per image, then Generate preview, 1 credit. That is 3 clicks after the install. The app showed Generating image 1 of 1 for about 70 seconds and, at about 21:54, a Generated result with the label 99% match, the buttons Image viewer, Download, Replace in Shopify and Regenerate, and the counter 24 credits available. The first result came about 2 minutes after the install. The result looked almost the same as the original: the same board and the same background, so no new studio scene was seen. The preview is labelled Private preview. Replace in Shopify was NOT clicked (it would change the product image), and Explore a new scene was not tried. The app has no storefront block, so no theme preview or app embed applies. Credits: the Billing screen still showed 25 credits and Credits used 0 after the preview, while the Studio screen showed 24 credits available. Billing shows the plan Free with an included allowance of 25 lifetime image generations, a ledger line Free plan, 25 lifetime image generations, plus 25, and the buttons Buy credits and Choose a plan. Plans: the plan window Choose the right plan lists Free (25 lifetime image generations), Starter $9 a month (75 credits, 30 day verified backups), Growth $29 a month (300 credits, 90 day), Pro $79 a month (1000 credits, 180 day) and Scale $199 a month (2500 credits, 365 day), with an Annual option that saves 15%, and the text Every new store receives 25 free image generations. The prices match the dossier. Checkout: a click on Choose monthly for Starter opened the Shopify page Select a plan with only the Free plan (Free to test: these plans are free to test on this store; Regular pricing applies when the store goes live). The paid plans were not selectable, no approval screen came up, no test charge was approved and no card was asked. The Select button of the Free plan was not clicked. Listing: the App Store listing (English) shows Pricing Free and a rating of 5.0 with 1 review, dated 6 September 2026. The dossier said the app had no reviews; that differs. Cancelling: no paid plan was started. In Settings, Apps, the menu of LumenCart offers Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall LumenCart? says that you can no longer use the app and that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and has a field Reason for uninstalling and a Share feedback box. Cancel was chosen first; our notes say that the uninstall was carried out after the session had been processed. Not tested: Replace in Shopify and publishing, Explore a new scene, Highest quality (2 credits), bulk generation, Brand, Backups, Catalogue, credit packs, the annual plans, the paid plans, and the group of stores that make thousands of images each month. Clean up: no product was created, nothing was published and no theme was changed. The price fields are not changed here. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The one preview we made looked almost identical to the original photo, so we saw no new studio scene. The Billing screen still showed 25 credits and 0 used while the Studio showed 24 credits. The paid plans of the app were not selectable on the Shopify plan page of our development store, which listed only Free.
